title: Choose between hosted and self-hosted models
summary: Use a requirements-led decision path to choose a hosted or self-hosted model deployment and record evidence for the choice.
prerequisites: An intended model workload and its operational requirements
Named owners for security, privacy, reliability, and budget decisions

sections.title: Decision and source update
paragraphs: Should you use a hosted or self-hosted model? For this intermediate-level guide, choose hosted operation when an external operating boundary satisfies your documented requirements and your team does not need to operate the serving environment. Choose self-hosted operation when your requirements demand control of that environment and your team can demonstrate that it can operate the full lifecycle. If either condition lacks evidence, do not decide yet. Record the gap as UNKNOWN and run a bounded evaluation or obtain the missing evidence.

In this guide, hosted means that another organization operates the model-serving environment. Self-hosted means that your organization operates that environment. These definitions describe operational responsibility, not a guarantee about security, privacy, cost, performance, or reliability.

The changed citation was content/resources/model-provider-decisions/hosted-vs-self-hosted-model-decision.json. It reached this review with an unregistered publisher and no prior verification, and it was not a resolvable HTTPS publisher source. It has therefore been removed from the source list and replaced with the cited risk-management source. The correction affects citation provenance and the guidance for documenting and verifying evidence. The decision path itself is unchanged.
sections.callout: This is a source-cadence correction. No provider, tool, version, or configuration-specific recommendation has been added.

sections.title: Decision procedure
paragraphs: Step one is to write the non-negotiable requirements for the intended workload. Cover the permitted data boundary, access control, monitoring, incident response, availability, capacity, maintenance ownership, and budget boundary. Name an owner and acceptable evidence for each requirement. If a requirement or owner is unclear, stop that part of the comparison and ask the accountable stakeholder to define it. Do not convert an unresolved requirement into an assumption.

Step two is to collect comparable evidence for both operating models. For hosted operation, document the responsibility boundary and the evidence available from the organization operating the environment. For self-hosted operation, document who will deploy, secure, monitor, update, scale, recover, and retire the environment. If evidence cannot be obtained or verified, label that item UNKNOWN and either request evidence, exclude the option, or test the item in a bounded evaluation.

Step three is to compare both options against the same requirements, workload, time period, and responsibility boundaries. Do not treat an omitted responsibility as zero effort or zero cost. If the two options use incompatible assumptions, normalize the assumptions and repeat the comparison. If normalization is not possible, retain the result as UNKNOWN and do not present a preferred option.

Step four is to choose only an option that passes every non-negotiable requirement with traceable evidence. Use the remaining criteria to distinguish options that pass. If neither option passes, revise the workload or requirements with the accountable owners rather than selecting the least incomplete option. If both pass but the result is too close to justify, run a bounded evaluation with predefined success and stop conditions. If that evaluation cannot be performed within the approved data and risk boundaries, defer the decision and escalate the unresolved boundary.

sections.title: Expected result and verification
paragraphs: The expected result is a decision record that names the selected operating model, lists the non-negotiable requirements, links each conclusion to evidence, identifies every UNKNOWN, assigns owners, records the rationale, and states what event will trigger review.

Verify the result by tracing every non-negotiable requirement to current evidence and an accountable owner. Confirm that hosted and self-hosted options were assessed with the same workload and responsibility boundaries. If a conclusion has no evidence, return to evidence collection. If the comparison uses different assumptions, normalize them and repeat it.

The decision is complete only when the selected option passes all non-negotiable requirements and the remaining uncertainty is explicitly accepted by an accountable owner. If an UNKNOWN could change whether an option passes, the decision is not complete. Obtain evidence, run the bounded evaluation, revise the requirement through the accountable owner, or defer the decision.
